audit_meta.scope: 38 thematic RE lessons (AQA + Unity): Theme A, B, C, D, E, F

findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: Wrong verse cited for Islamic ensoulment / sanctity of life. The lesson opens: 'Muslims believe Allah breathes a soul into every person: "It is He who created you from clay, then determined a term for you" (Qur'an 6:2).' Qur'an 6:2 (Al-An'am) is about lifespan/appointed death-term, NOT about soul-breathing or ensoulment. The soul-breathing verse is Qur'an 32:9 ('Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul'). This is the same 6:2 error that was corrected in the AQA version but survived in the Unity parallel lesson.
findings.expected: Qur'an 32:9 for soul-breathing; the euthanasia predestination point (lifespan determined by Allah) could legitimately cite 3:145 or 6:2 if framed correctly as 'lifespan is divinely appointed', but NOT as the soul-breathing / sanctity-of-life anchor.
findings.note: The AQA sibling lesson (fee82fde) correctly distinguishes: it uses 32:9 for ensoulment and then explicitly parenthesises 6:2 as the lifespan verse. The Unity L3 lesson conflates them.

findings.lesson_title: Punishment: Aims, Types & the Death Penalty
findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: Wrong verse cited for reformation/repentance. The lesson states: 'Islam also supports reformation – the Qur'an teaches: "But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness" (5:39).' Qur'an 5:39 does say this, but the context is the verse immediately following the hadd punishment for theft (5:38), so using 5:39 to support prison-style reformation is technically valid — HOWEVER the same lesson cites 5:45 for lex talionis retribution ('We ordained for them: a life for a life, an eye for an eye'). Qur'an 5:45 is specifically about the Torah's lex talionis as recorded in the Qur'an, not a general Qur'anic endorsement of retribution. The lesson presents 5:45 as a straightforward Islamic teaching without noting its Torah-citation framing ('We ordained for them [the Children of Israel] in the Torah').
findings.expected: 5:45 should be attributed as 'what the Qur'an records the Torah as prescribing for the Children of Israel' rather than a first-person Qur'anic rule for Muslims. This same misattribution appears in the AQA sibling (3c28f2ae) — both are affected.
findings.note: Both AQA and Unity punishment lessons have this framing issue with 5:45. Severity HIGH because it misattributes a Torah law to Islamic teaching.

findings.lesson_title: Punishment: Aims, Types & the Death Penalty
findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: Same 5:45 Torah-citation misattribution as THM-002. The lesson states: 'In Islam, the Qur'an also permits retribution: "We ordained for them: a life for a life, an eye for an eye" (5:45).' The phrase 'We ordained for them' refers specifically to the Children of Israel as recorded in the Torah. Presenting this as a general Islamic rule for retribution is doctrinally inaccurate.
findings.expected: Use Qur'an 2:178 or explain 5:45's Torah-citation context. Alternatively note that Islamic law does recognise qisas (retaliation) but source it from its own tradition rather than this particular verse.
findings.note: Parallel to THM-002; both lessons built from same template.

findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: Mistranslation / wrong doctrinal use. The lesson quotes: '"Do not kill each other, for God is merciful to you" (Qur'an 4:29)' to support an Islamic prohibition of euthanasia. Qur'an 4:29 in all standard translations says 'do not kill yourselves [or one another]' — it is primarily a prohibition of suicide and mutual killing, not euthanasia specifically, and the full verse opens with a prohibition on consuming each other's wealth unjustly. While scholars do apply 4:29 to euthanasia analogically, presenting 'do not kill each other' as the direct quoted text is a paraphrase that somewhat misrepresents the verse's actual wording ('do not kill yourselves / one another'). More importantly the verse is about suicide/mutual killing in the context of consuming each other's wealth — not a euthanasia verse. A MEDIUM issue rather than HIGH except that this already has a correct alternative (3:145) cited immediately before it in the same sentence.
findings.expected: Better to use Qur'an 17:33 ('do not take life which Allah has made sacred, except by right') which is more directly applicable and accurately quoted in the death penalty lesson.
findings.note: Downgrade to MEDIUM given 3:145 is already present in the same sentence and carries the point correctly.

findings.lesson_title: Nuclear Weapons and Weapons of Mass Destruction
findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: Inaccurate paraphrase cited as direct quotation. The lesson states: 'The Qur'an states: "If you have to respond to an attack, make your response proportionate" (Qur'an 2:194).' Qur'an 2:194 is about retaliation specifically in the sacred months (the Hajj period): 'A sacred month for a sacred month, and [all] violations will bring about retaliation. So, if anyone attacks you, retaliate in the same manner.' It is not a general proportionality principle and does not use the phrasing 'make your response proportionate.' The lesson's version is a paraphrase that erases the sacred-month context and creates a wording not found in any standard translation.
findings.expected: The general proportionality principle in Islam is better sourced from Qur'an 2:190 ('Fight in the way of God those who fight you, but do not transgress') which is correctly quoted elsewhere in the same unit.
findings.note: The AQA WMD lesson (18dc29a8) omits Qur'anic verse citations entirely — no error there. Only the Unity L4 has this problem.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: Although this lesson correctly handles 6:2 (explicitly framing it as the lifespan verse, not the ensoulment verse), the juxtaposition is still potentially confusing for GCSE students. The lesson first cites Qur'an 32:9 for ensoulment, then immediately adds 6:2 in parentheses as additional support for the sanctity argument. Because 6:2 is about lifespan/appointed death-term ('determined a term for you'), using it alongside 32:9 in the sanctity-of-life context could mislead students into thinking 6:2 also supports ensoulment.
findings.expected: Minor editorial clarification: separate the 6:2 citation and make its distinct doctrinal role explicit. The information is not wrong but the proximity invites conflation.
findings.note: LOW-MEDIUM: the AQA lesson is more careful than the Unity version, but could still be clearer.

findings.lesson_title: War: Just War, Holy War & Pacifism
findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson lists seven just war criteria and attributes them to Aquinas ('developed by Christian thinkers, most notably St Thomas Aquinas in the 13th century'). However Aquinas's own Summa Theologiae (II-II Q.40) lists only three conditions (sovereign authority, just cause, right intention). The seven-criteria version is a modern Catholic development found in the 1992 Catechism (CCC 2309) and twentieth-century just war scholarship. The lesson conflates Aquinas's historical framework with modern Catholic teaching.
findings.expected: Either attribute the seven criteria to 'the just war tradition developed by Aquinas and elaborated by the Catholic Church' or name the Catechism as the modern source. This is a medium error because the criteria themselves are accurate — only the attribution is conflated.
findings.note: Same conflation appears in the Unity parallel lesson (0057965b) — both affected.

findings.lesson_title: War: Just War, Holy War & Pacifism
findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: Same Aquinas/Catechism attribution conflation as THM-007. Unity parallel lesson.
findings.expected: Same fix as THM-007.
findings.note: Parallel to THM-007.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.citation: MLK Letter from Birmingham Jail — Aquinas/Augustine attribution
findings.issue: The lesson correctly attributes the Letter from Birmingham Jail to MLK and correctly notes his references to Augustine and Aquinas on just vs unjust laws. No inaccuracy here. HOWEVER, the lesson says King 'drew on the natural-law tradition rooted in Augustine and Aquinas' — this is accurate. The lesson also references the 'beloved community' vision, which is correct. No error found — upgrading to LOW.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Pre-emptive check passed — no error. Removing from HIGH findings list, keeping as reviewed.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson correctly cites Qur'an 4:3 for polygamy ('Islam permits a man to have up to four wives (Qur'an 4:3), provided he treats each wife equally') and correctly cites 4:129 for the caveat. This is accurate. However, the lesson omits that 4:3 was revealed in the specific context of protecting orphan women's property rights after the Battle of Uhud — the verse begins 'If you fear you might fail to give orphan women their due rights, then marry other women'. This contextual omission is a doctrinal oversimplification rather than an error, but it matters at GCSE level where students should understand the contextual basis of Qur'anic rulings.
findings.expected: A sentence noting the orphan-welfare context would improve doctrinal accuracy. The citation itself is correct.
findings.note: Same pattern in Unity L2 (67c8b94d) — both omit context. LOW-MEDIUM.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson quotes Qur'an 50:16 as: '"closer to you than your jugular vein".' This is an accurate quotation. However, the lesson uses it to illustrate divine immanence, stating 'Most monotheistic traditions hold that God is both — "closer to you than your jugular vein" (Qur'an 50:16) and yet beyond full human comprehension.' Qur'an 50:16 in full is: 'Indeed, We created mankind and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein.' The verse is actually about Allah's omniscience (knowing human thoughts), not primarily about immanence vs transcendence. Using it as a general immanence proof-text is a doctrinal oversimplification. MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the lesson's use is not factually wrong — the verse does express divine closeness.
findings.expected: Acknowledge that the verse's primary point is omniscience, with divine closeness as the supporting image.
findings.note: Common GCSE textbook usage; not unique to this lesson.

findings.lesson_title: Wealth, Poverty and the Uses of Money
findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson states: 'The Quran explicitly forbids riba (Quran 2:275), stating that those who consume interest will arise on the Day of Judgement as those who have been touched by Satan.' This is an accurate rendering of 2:275. However the lesson adds 'This prohibition is grounded in the belief that charging interest exploits those in financial difficulty and concentrates wealth unjustly.' While this is a valid theological explanation given by many scholars, it is NOT stated in 2:275 itself — the verse prohibits riba but does not explain the reason in these terms. The lesson presents this rationale as if it derives from the verse.
findings.expected: Separate the Qur'anic citation from the scholarly rationale: 'Scholars explain this prohibition as rooted in...' rather than attributing the reasoning to 2:275 directly.
findings.note: Minor editorial issue — LOW-MEDIUM.

findings.lesson_title: Peacemaking and Responses to Victims of War
findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: The lesson quotes: '"Whoever has saved a life, it is as though he has saved the whole of mankind" (Surah 5:32)' to support Muslim duties to protect war victims. While the sentiment is theologically appropriate, Qur'an 5:32 in full is: 'That is why We ordained for the Children of Israel that whoever takes a life — unless as punishment for murder or mischief in the land — it is as if they killed all of humanity.' Like the 5:45 problem (THM-002/003), this verse is framed as what was ordained 'for the Children of Israel' — it is a Qur'anic reference to a Torah ruling, not a direct Qur'anic injunction to Muslims. The lesson uses it as a direct Islamic injunction without this qualification.
findings.expected: Note the Children of Israel framing. The theological principle of life's sanctity can be supported by other Qur'anic verses that are direct injunctions (e.g., 6:151, 17:33). Many scholars and GCSE sources use 5:32 in this universal sense, making this a widespread but technically imprecise usage.
findings.note: This same issue appears in the AQA Environment lesson (4ddc74fe) where 5:32 is quoted for animal experimentation. Also in Unity Abortion L4. All three instances have this framing omission.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: Same Children of Israel framing omission as THM-013. The lesson quotes 5:32 ('Whoever saves a life, it is as if he has saved all of humanity') to support Muslim acceptance of animal experimentation for medical advances. The verse is about human life specifically (ordained for the Children of Israel), not a general principle about saving lives that would extend to animal experimentation.
findings.expected: Use a more appropriate verse (e.g., Hadith on necessity/darurah) or acknowledge the Children of Israel context.
findings.note: Parallel to THM-013.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson quotes Qur'an 22:39 as: '"Those who have been attacked are permitted to take up arms".' Standard translations read: 'Permission [to fight back] is granted to those being fought, for they have been wronged' (Sahih International) or 'Permission to fight back is granted to those being fought' (Khattab). The lesson's version ('permitted to take up arms') is a reasonable paraphrase that captures the meaning accurately. LOW — wording variation only.
findings.expected: Acceptable paraphrase; no correction required.
findings.note: Same phrasing used consistently across AQA and Unity peace lessons — internally consistent.

findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: Same LOW paraphrase variation as THM-015.
findings.expected: No correction required.
findings.note: Parallel to THM-015.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson's Key Fact states: 'The Qur'an (30:21) describes marriage as a source of "love and mercy".' This is accurate and standard. No error. PASS.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean.

findings.lesson_title: Human Rights, Equality and Freedom of Religion
findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson cites Qur'an 17:70 for 'the dignity God conferred on all humans' in the Key Fact. Qur'an 17:70 reads: 'Indeed We have honoured the children of Adam, and carried them by land and sea, and provided them with good things, and preferred them over much of what We have created.' This is a correct citation for human dignity — clean.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean.

findings.lesson_title: Origins of the Universe & Human Life
findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson cites Surah 21:30: '"The heavens and the earth were joined together, then We split them apart"' as a Big Bang parallel. This is an accurate quotation and a standard interpretation. No error.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean.

findings.lesson_title: Arguments For the Existence of God
findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson says Aquinas presented his First Cause argument in Summa Theologiae and describes it as 'the second of his Five Ways addresses causation.' The First Cause / Causation argument is actually Aquinas's SECOND Way in Summa Theologiae II-II Q.3 (the first being the Unmoved Mover). The lesson correctly identifies it as the second Way — this is accurate. PASS.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean — Second Way correctly identified.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.citation: Qur'an 3:190 — signs for those who reason
findings.issue: The lesson quotes: '"In the creation of the heavens and earth... there are signs for those who reason" (Qur'an 3:190).' Standard translation (Khattab): 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the day and night there are signs for people of reason.' Accurate — clean.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean. Note: the lesson does not cite Qur'an 41:53 ('We will show them Our signs in the horizons') which would be a natural addition for the existence-of-God theme but its absence is not an error.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson quotes: '"Whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah" (42:40).' Standard translation (Sahih International): 'whoever pardons and makes reconciliation — his reward is [due] from Allah.' This is accurate. PASS.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean. Same citation used consistently across AQA and Unity forgiveness lessons.

findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: The lesson cites Surah 17:33 twice with two different apparent quotations: (1) 'Do not take life, which Allah has made sacred, except by right' and (2) 'If anyone is killed unjustly, we have granted the right of retribution to his heir'. Both are from the same verse — 17:33 contains both clauses. The lesson presents them as two separate quotes from the same reference, which is accurate to the verse's bipartite structure. This is correct usage but could confuse students into thinking they are separate verses. LOW.
findings.expected: Clarify that both clauses come from the same single verse.
findings.note: Not an error per se, but pedagogically unclear.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson quotes Galatians 3:28: '"There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus".' This is an accurate NIV rendering. PASS.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean.

findings.subject: religious-studies-unity
findings.issue: The lesson quotes: '"People, We created you all from a single man and a single woman, and made you into races and tribes so that you could recognise one another" (Qur'an 49:13).' Standard translations say 'from a male and a female' (not 'a single man and a single woman'). The lesson's version is a paraphrase that is slightly more wordy but not inaccurate in meaning. LOW wording variation.
findings.expected: Minor: prefer 'from a male and a female' to match standard translation more closely.
findings.note: Clean in substance.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson quotes: '"Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it" (Qur'an 99:7-8).' This is an accurate translation of Az-Zalzalah 7-8. PASS.
findings.expected: No correction needed.
findings.note: Verified clean.

findings.subject: religious-studies-aqa
findings.issue: The lesson correctly attributes soul-breathing to Qur'an 32:9 and quotes it in context as 'Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His Spirit.' Standard translations: 'Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul.' The lesson's version is a valid translation (Pickthall/older translators render 'of His Spirit'). PASS.
findings.expected: No correction needed. The AQA version handles 6:2 vs 32:9 correctly.
findings.note: Verified clean. This is the corrected version; the Unity L3 (THM-001) was NOT fixed.

top_5_worst_lessons.title: Abortion & Euthanasia (Unity L3)
top_5_worst_lessons.reason: THM-001: Uses Qur'an 6:2 (lifespan verse) as the soul-breathing/sanctity-of-life anchor — the exact error corrected in the AQA sibling but surviving in the Unity version. Misleads students on Islamic ensoulment doctrine.

top_5_worst_lessons.title: Punishment: Aims, Types & Death Penalty (Unity L2)
top_5_worst_lessons.reason: THM-002: Qur'an 5:45 ('We ordained for them [the Children of Israel]: a life for a life') presented as a general Islamic retribution rule. The verse is a Qur'anic record of a Torah ruling, not a direct Islamic law.

top_5_worst_lessons.title: Punishment: Aims, Types & Death Penalty (AQA L2)
top_5_worst_lessons.reason: THM-003: Same 5:45 Torah-citation misattribution as rank 2. Both punishment lessons need the same fix.

top_5_worst_lessons.title: Nuclear Weapons and WMD (Unity L4)
top_5_worst_lessons.reason: THM-005: Qur'an 2:194 paraphrased as 'make your response proportionate' but the verse is specifically about retaliation in the sacred Hajj months, not a general proportionality principle.

top_5_worst_lessons.title: Peacemaking and Responses to Victims of War (Unity L5)
top_5_worst_lessons.reason: THM-013: Qur'an 5:32 ('whoever saves a life') cited as a direct Islamic injunction but the verse is framed as ordained 'for the Children of Israel' — a Torah ruling referenced in the Qur'an, not a direct Qur'anic command to Muslims.

cross_cutting_issues: Qur'an 5:32 and 5:45 both have the same structural problem: they are Qur'anic records of Torah rulings ('We ordained for the Children of Israel / for them in the Torah') but are cited in three lessons as direct Islamic injunctions. This pattern affects AQA Environment (5:32), AQA Punishment (5:45), Unity Punishment (5:45), and Unity Peacemaking (5:32).

The AQA Abortion lesson (fee82fde) correctly fixed the 6:2 vs 32:9 ensoulment issue but the Unity parallel (3f8e7f3a) was not updated — confirming the correction was made only in one of two sibling lessons.
Both AQA and Unity Just War lessons conflate Aquinas's three conditions with the modern seven-criteria list from the 1992 Catholic Catechism — a widespread GCSE textbook error.
